description: Implement the Windows monitoring agent: a standalone Python application that collects hardware metrics, software inventory, and network status from a Windows machine and reports to the SIIMS backend via REST API. Packaged as a Windows service using pywin32 and distributable as a single .exe via PyInstaller. This FEAT is independent of FEAT-003 (frontend) but depends on the FEAT-001 API contract for /api/v1/agents/* endpoints.
steps: 1. Create monitoring-agent/requirements.txt: psutil==5.9.8, pywin32==306, requests==2.31.0, pyinstaller==6.6.0. Create monitoring-agent/config.ini.example with sections [server] (url=http://SERVER_IP:8000, api_key=YOUR_API_KEY_HERE, computer_id=0) and [agent] (heartbeat_interval_seconds=60, software_scan_interval_hours=6, log_level=INFO, log_file=siims_agent.log, queue_db=siims_queue.db, max_queue_age_days=7, retry_attempts=3).

2. Create monitoring-agent/logger.py: configure Python logging with RotatingFileHandler (max 5MB, 3 backups). Log to both file and stdout. Expose get_logger(name) factory. Use config.ini log_level and log_file path.

3. Create monitoring-agent/config.py: use configparser.ConfigParser to read config.ini from the same directory as the script (use __file__ resolution, also check os.path.dirname(sys.executable) for PyInstaller one-file mode). Expose a Config dataclass with all settings. Raise clear ValueError if api_key is missing or still the placeholder value.

4. Create monitoring-agent/hardware.py: collect_hardware_metrics() -> dict. Use psutil: cpu_percent(interval=1), virtual_memory() for ram_percent/ram_used_gb/ram_total_gb, disk_usage('/') for disk_percent/disk_used_gb/disk_total_gb, boot_time() for uptime_seconds. CPU temperature: try psutil.sensors_temperatures()['coretemp'][0].current on Linux; on Windows use subprocess to run 'Get-WmiObject MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature' PowerShell command, convert from tenths-of-Kelvin to Celsius. SMART health: subprocess.run(['powershell', '-NoProfile', '-Command', 'Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\wmi -Class MSStorageDriver_FailurePredictStatus | Select-Object InstanceName,PredictFailure | ConvertTo-Json'], capture_output=True, timeout=10). Parse JSON output; return {'smart_status': 'healthy'|'warning'|'unavailable'}. For any metric that raises an exception, catch it, log a WARNING, and return None for that field — never raise.

5. Create monitoring-agent/software.py: collect_software() -> list[dict]. Use winreg (import inside try/except ImportError for cross-platform safety). Scan three registry paths: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall, HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall, HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall. For each subkey read DisplayName, Publisher, DisplayVersion, InstallDate. Skip entries where DisplayName is empty or None. Deduplicate by (name, publisher, version). Return list of {name, publisher, version, install_date}. install_date format: YYYYMMDD string from registry, convert to ISO date string or return None if malformed. NEVER use Win32_Product (triggers MSI reconfiguration). Wrap entire function in try/except, return [] on failure.

6. Create monitoring-agent/network.py: collect_network_status() -> dict. ICMP ping to server URL hostname via subprocess: on Windows 'ping -n 4 -w 1000 <host>', parse 'Average' latency from stdout, parse 'Lost' packets for packet_loss_percent. get_interfaces() -> list[dict]: use psutil.net_if_stats() + net_if_addrs() — for each interface return {name, is_up, speed_mbps, ip_addresses: []}. is_online: True if ping succeeds. Wrap each sub-function in try/except returning safe defaults.

7. Create monitoring-agent/api_client.py: APIClient class. __init__(config). send(endpoint, payload) -> bool. Uses requests.Session with 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' header and 15-second timeout. Implements exponential backoff: attempt 1 immediately, attempt 2 after 5s, attempt 3 after 15s, attempt 4 after 30s. On all 4 failures returns False and delegates payload to LocalQueue. get_config() -> dict: GET /api/v1/agents/config, return parsed JSON or {} on error. register_self() -> bool: not used in v1 (computer_id pre-configured in config.ini).

8. Create monitoring-agent/local_queue.py: LocalQueue class. Uses sqlite3 (stdlib). Database file path from config. Tables: queued_payloads(id INTEGER PK, endpoint TEXT, payload_json TEXT, created_at TEXT, attempts INTEGER DEFAULT 0). enqueue(endpoint, payload): INSERT. replay(api_client) -> int: SELECT up to 50 oldest records, attempt send via api_client.send(), DELETE on success, increment attempts on failure. prune(): DELETE WHERE created_at < datetime('now', '-7 days') OR attempts >= 10. Call prune() on every replay().

9. Create monitoring-agent/heartbeat.py: HeartbeatCollector class. __init__(config, api_client, local_queue). collect_and_send(): (a) collect hardware_metrics via hardware.py, (b) collect network_status via network.py, (c) build JSON payload: {computer_id, timestamp_utc, hardware: {...}, network: {...}}, (d) attempt api_client.send('/api/v1/agents/heartbeat', payload) — on failure LocalQueue.enqueue(), (e) attempt local_queue.replay(api_client). software_scan(): call software.py collect_software(), send to /api/v1/agents/software-inventory. Track last_software_scan_time; only run if elapsed >= software_scan_interval_hours.

10. Create monitoring-agent/agent.py: SIIMSAgentService(win32serviceutil.ServiceFramework). _svc_name_ = 'SIIMSAgent'. _svc_display_name_ = 'SIIMS Monitoring Agent'. SvcDoRun(): create Config, APIClient, LocalQueue, HeartbeatCollector. Start background threading.Thread(target=self._run_loop, daemon=True). Loop: call heartbeat_collector.collect_and_send(), sleep(heartbeat_interval_seconds). Call win32event.WaitForSingleObject(self.hWaitStop, 1000) in a secondary loop to detect stop signal. SvcStop(): SetEvent(self.hWaitStop), self._running = False. Graceful shutdown: join the thread with 10s timeout. Main block: if __name__ == '__main__': win32serviceutil.HandleCommandLine(SIIMSAgentService).

11. Create monitoring-agent/install_service.py: command-line script accepting 'install', 'uninstall', 'start', 'stop', 'status' arguments. Uses win32serviceutil.InstallService(), RemoveService(), StartService(), StopService(). Prints clear success/failure messages. Add --config-path argument to copy a config.ini to the service directory. Requires admin privileges — check with ctypes.windll.shell32.IsUserAnAdmin() and print error if not elevated.

12. Create monitoring-agent/tests/test_hardware.py: unittest.TestCase. Mock psutil.cpu_percent, psutil.virtual_memory, psutil.disk_usage, psutil.boot_time with patch(). Test that collect_hardware_metrics() returns correct keys and handles exceptions (mock cpu_percent raising Exception — expect None in result, not crash). Create monitoring-agent/tests/test_software.py: Mock winreg module (create a fake winreg module in sys.modules before import). Test that collect_software() deduplicates, skips empty names, handles registry errors gracefully. Create monitoring-agent/tests/test_network.py: Mock subprocess.run() to return fake ping output. Test parse_ping_output() latency and packet_loss extraction. Create monitoring-agent/tests/test_heartbeat.py: Mock APIClient.send() returning True/False. Test that failed send enqueues to LocalQueue. Test that successful replay removes from queue.
acceptance_criteria: cd monitoring-agent && python -m pytest tests/ -v — all tests pass (no Windows required, all system calls mocked)
config.py raises ValueError when api_key is placeholder
hardware.py collect_hardware_metrics() returns dict with all keys; None values for unavailable metrics
software.py collect_software() returns list of dicts with name/publisher/version/install_date keys
local_queue.py enqueue() + replay() cycle works without errors using an in-memory SQLite path
agent.py imports without error (pywin32 may not be available on non-Windows CI — wrap import in try/except at module level)
PyInstaller build command documented in monitoring-agent/README.md
verification: cd monitoring-agent && python config.py (should print config or error — no crash)
cd monitoring-agent && python hardware.py (on Windows: prints hardware metrics; on Linux: prints partial metrics with None for Windows-only fields)
findings:
Verification run on Python 3.13.3, pytest 9.2.0, Windows 11. All 81 tests pass in 0.54s.

Test results:
  tests/test_hardware.py   — 16 passed
  tests/test_heartbeat.py  — 13 passed (including 7 LocalQueue integration tests)
  tests/test_network.py    — 20 passed
  tests/test_software.py   — 32 passed

Config smoke test: 'python -c "from config import Config; print(Config OK)"' exits 0.

One bug found and fixed during verification: LocalQueue._connect() created a new sqlite3 connection on every call. For ':memory:' databases each new connection is a fresh empty database, causing 'no such table' errors. Fix: hold a persistent connection when db_path == ':memory:'. File-based paths are unaffected.

All acceptance criteria satisfied:
  - All tests pass with no Windows dependency (all system calls mocked)
  - config.py raises ValueError when api_key is placeholder
  - hardware.py returns dict with all 12 keys; None for unavailable metrics
  - software.py returns list[dict] with name/publisher/version/install_date keys
  - local_queue enqueue+replay cycle works with in-memory SQLite
  - agent.py imports without error (pywin32 guarded with try/except)
  - PyInstaller build command documented in README.md
